studies.name: EXPERTS-ALS
studies.blurb: Screens candidate drugs quickly by measuring neurofilament light chain in blood. Currently testing metformin, nifedipine and ropinirole, with neflamapimod and smilagenin announced for later arms. Everyone who joins receives a drug. A further drug, RT1999, is expected to be added to the platform by the end of 2026.
studies.plain: In plain terms: these are existing drugs, already licensed for other conditions, being re-tested in MND. The trial doesn't measure whether people feel better — it measures whether a protein in the blood called neurofilament light, which rises as nerve cells are damaged, falls while the drug is taken. That makes it a fast screen rather than proof of benefit: a positive result means the drug earns a bigger trial, not that it slows the disease. Most drugs tested this way do not go forward.
studies.burden: 6 visits over 6 months, blood samples at each
studies.apply: Rolling — referral through his neurology team
studies.barLabel: Rolling · referral any time · 17 UK sites

criteria.text: Riluzole allowed if the dose is stable
Respiratory function above the trial threshold
criteria.unknownNote: no recent FVC on record — the clinic will have one

criteria.text: Under the care of a participating centre
criteria.note: only his team can confirm this

studies.name: MND-SMART
studies.blurb: Adaptive platform run from Edinburgh. Amantadine was discontinued in March 2026 after showing no benefit, so tacrolimus is now the only active arm. A further drug is expected to be added later in 2026.
studies.plain: In plain terms: tacrolimus is an immune-damping drug used after transplants. The theory is that some of the nerve damage in MND is driven by the body's own immune activity, so quietening it might slow the loss of function. This is a proper efficacy trial with a placebo group, so it can genuinely detect a slowing — but a realistic hope is a modest change in the rate of decline, not a reversal. With amantadine now dropped, roughly half of new participants will receive placebo rather than tacrolimus.
studies.burden: Monthly contact, mostly remote after the first visits
studies.apply: Rolling — referral through his neurology team, but you can register interest yourselves first

criteria.text: No limit on time since diagnosis
Not dependent on ventilation for most of the day

studies.name: PREVAiLS · pridopidine
studies.blurb: Confirmatory phase 3 of pridopidine. The first participant was enrolled in early 2026 and sites are opening in waves across 13 countries including the UK, so availability at a given centre changes month to month.
studies.plain: In plain terms: pridopidine acts on the sigma-1 receptor, a switch inside nerve cells that helps them cope with stress and keep their long fibres healthy. An earlier trial missed its main target overall but hinted at benefit in people early in the disease and not yet using breathing support — which is who this trial is aimed at. Best case is a slower decline over six months; the honest expectation is uncertain.
studies.burden: Clinic visits every 4 weeks, breathing tests at each
studies.apply: Closes 31 Oct 2026 — referral needed by early September

criteria.blockedShort: not open to people already using NIV

criteria.note: published only in the full protocol

studies.name: FUSION · ulefnersen
studies.blurb: For people with a FUS gene fault only. Not listed by the UK Clinical Studies Group, so any UK access would be through a genetics centre rather than a standard trial referral.
studies.plain: In plain terms: this is the most targeted kind of treatment available in MND. Where a FUS gene fault is the cause, the gene issues a damaging instruction; ulefnersen is designed to silence that instruction before the harmful protein is made. Individual patients treated early have shown striking stabilisation, so expectations here are higher than for most trials — but it only applies to the small number of people whose disease is caused by that gene.
studies.apply: Referral via a specialist genetic MND clinic

criteria.text: Confirmed change in the FUS gene
Able to attend a specialist centre for lumbar punctures
criteria.note: depends on travel and his wishes

studies.name: Tofersen early access
studies.blurb: Free-of-charge access to tofersen for the roughly 2% of people whose MND is caused by a fault in the SOD1 gene, while NHS commissioning is decided. Capacity depends on the care centre.
studies.plain: In plain terms: the same silencing approach as ulefnersen, but for the SOD1 gene. Tofersen lowers the harmful SOD1 protein and reduced neurofilament levels in trials; benefit to function appeared slowly and was clearest in people treated early. It is injected into the spine monthly, indefinitely. It is not a cure and does not recover function already lost.
studies.apply: Through an MND care centre able to deliver it

criteria.text: Confirmed change in the SOD1 gene
Care centre with capacity to deliver it

studies.name: FUNCtion ALS · TRCN-1023
studies.blurb: Opening at UK sites later this year. Criteria are not published yet — early-phase trials usually ask for a recent diagnosis, so it is worth raising before then.
studies.plain: In plain terms: an early-phase study, so its purpose is to establish safety and the right dose rather than to show benefit. Taking part is a contribution to the science more than a treatment plan.
studies.apply: Not yet open

studies.name: PIONEER-ALS · Vtx-002
studies.blurb: Gene therapy given as a single injection at the base of the brain, testing two doses in twelve people. VectorY received UK and European authorisation in April 2026 and the study is recruiting in the US and Europe, but the UK sites are still listed as in set-up. Twelve places worldwide makes this a long shot.
studies.plain: In plain terms: another early-phase safety and dosing study. Any effect on symptoms would be a bonus rather than the goal, and criteria usually favour people diagnosed recently.
studies.apply: Not yet open
studies.tlNote: UK sites in set-up · recruiting elsewhere

studies.name: Nura Bio · VNB-4746
studies.blurb: Phase 1b/2 study of VNB-4746 in ALS, in set-up in the UK.
studies.plain: In plain terms: VNB-4746 targets SARM1, an enzyme that acts as a self-destruct switch inside damaged nerve fibres. Blocking it is a genuinely new idea in MND, but this stage of testing is about safety and dose, not proof that it helps.
studies.apply: Not yet open

studies.name: ALS Biomarkers Study
studies.blurb: Builds a sample bank covering the natural history of the disease, using simple at-home collection kits. You can sign up yourselves without a referral.
studies.plain: In plain terms: no treatment is given. Samples are used to work out which markers in blood track the disease, so future trials can tell sooner whether a drug is working. It costs almost no time and makes better trials possible for others.
studies.burden: Occasional home sample kits by post
studies.apply: Sign up directly — no referral needed
studies.barLabel: Rolling · sign up yourselves, no travel

criteria.text: Able to give samples at home

studies.name: Join MND Research
studies.blurb: A register that matches people to studies they could take part in, locally and online. Signing up here means new studies find them, rather than the other way round.
studies.plain: In plain terms: not a study in itself — a way of being found. Researchers search the register when they need participants, so signing up means opportunities come to you rather than needing to be spotted.
studies.apply: Sign up directly — no referral needed

studies.name: MND Register
studies.blurb: National record of everyone living with MND in the UK, led from King's College London and Oxford. Consent is usually taken at a care centre.
studies.plain: In plain terms: a headcount, essentially. Knowing accurately how many people have MND and where they live shapes NHS funding and where trials are placed. No visits, no treatment, no burden.
studies.apply: Ask his care team to add him

criteria.text: Living with MND in the UK

studies.name: TONiC
studies.blurb: National questionnaire study on what shapes quality of life in neurological conditions. Runs at participating clinics only.
studies.plain: In plain terms: a questionnaire about what actually affects day-to-day quality of life — fatigue, mood, independence — rather than anything about drugs. It shapes how services are designed, and someone else can write the answers down for him.
studies.apply: Ask at his next clinic appointment

criteria.note: not listed publicly — ask the team

studies.name: DENIM
studies.blurb: Tests whether intensive support at home helps people use non-invasive ventilation for longer. Only open once NIV has been started, so worth revisiting later.
studies.plain: In plain terms: not a drug. It tests whether extra hands-on support at home helps people keep using their breathing machine comfortably, and for longer. NIV is one of the few things shown to help both survival and quality of life in MND, so getting good use of it matters more than most things on this list.
studies.burden: Home visits from the respiratory team
studies.apply: Through the respiratory or MND team

studies.name: ACORN
studies.blurb: Investigates nerve damage in people carrying a change in the C9orf72 gene, the most common genetic cause of MND.
studies.plain: In plain terms: an observational study tracking how nerve damage develops in people carrying the C9orf72 fault, to work out how early it begins. No treatment is given; it lays the groundwork for gene-targeted drugs like those now available for SOD1 and FUS.
studies.apply: Via a specialist genetic clinic

studies.name: MONITOR ALS
studies.blurb: Measures motor neurone activity non-invasively, looking for markers of progression that could replace more burdensome tests.
studies.plain: In plain terms: no treatment. It tests whether motor neurone activity can be measured without needles, so future trials could track progression more comfortably and with fewer participants.
studies.burden: Repeat recording sessions at the site
studies.apply: Ask his team for a referral

criteria.text: Able to travel to the study site
criteria.note: 160 miles — depends on what he'd find manageable

studies.name: Motor System Genomics
studies.blurb: Studies fluid samples from people with MND, family members and controls to find markers that aid diagnosis.
studies.plain: In plain terms: sample donation. The aim is to find markers that let MND be diagnosed sooner — diagnosis currently takes around a year on average, and that is time lost for trials that require an early diagnosis.
studies.burden: Blood or fluid samples at routine visits
studies.apply: Ask at his next appointment

criteria.text: His centre collects for this study

studies.name: MND microbiome study
studies.blurb: Compares gut microbial samples from people with MND, family members and healthy controls.
studies.plain: In plain terms: sample donation, looking at whether gut bacteria differ in people with MND. Exploratory work — interesting, unproven, and no burden to take part in.
studies.apply: Ask at his next appointment

criteria.text: His centre collects for this study

studies.name: MND GENETICS
studies.blurb: Genetically screens 150 people with MND and 50 family members to identify causative variants. Relevant even after standard testing, as the panel is wider.
studies.plain: In plain terms: broader genetic testing than the standard NHS panel. Worth knowing about even though standard testing found nothing, because a wider panel occasionally finds a variant — and a known variant can open the door to gene-targeted trials that are otherwise closed.
studies.apply: Ask his team about a referral

studies.name: Measuring muscle health in MND
studies.blurb: Uses ultrasound to measure muscle health, aiming at earlier diagnosis and better monitoring.
studies.plain: In plain terms: painless ultrasound scans of muscle, to see whether they show change earlier than current measures. No treatment is given.
studies.apply: Ask at his next appointment

studies.name: CAS-MND
studies.blurb: Looks at how people with MND and their carers manage coughing and excess saliva or phlegm, and what gets in the way of managing it well.
studies.plain: In plain terms: not a drug. Interviews and questionnaires about a symptom that becomes a daily problem for most people with MND. It won't change his own care, but it feeds directly into guidance that would.
studies.site: Remote — by phone, video or questionnaire
studies.burden: Interview or questionnaire, one or two sessions
studies.apply: Sign up through your MND team, or ask them to refer you

studies.name: Management of choking
studies.blurb: Explores choking episodes in people living with MND and is developing treatment guidance for teams managing them.
studies.plain: In plain terms: not a drug. It gathers real accounts of choking episodes so that clear guidance can be written for clinical teams. Low burden, and directly relevant if swallowing becomes an issue.
studies.site: Remote — by phone, video or questionnaire
studies.apply: Sign up through your MND team, or ask them to refer you

studies.name: MND Together
studies.blurb: Examines what works and what fails in the coordination of MND services across the NHS and social care.
studies.plain: In plain terms: not a drug. It's about the joins between services — the neurologist, the respiratory team, community care — and where they come apart. Useful to contribute to if the care coordination has been frustrating.
studies.site: Remote — by phone, video or questionnaire
studies.apply: Sign up through your MND team, or ask them to refer you

studies.name: Opti MND
studies.blurb: Compares different ways of delivering MND care and how they affect outcomes for both the person with MND and their family carers.
studies.plain: In plain terms: not a drug. It follows how different care setups play out, including for carers — one of the few studies that treats the family's experience as an outcome in its own right.
studies.site: Remote — by phone, video or questionnaire
studies.apply: Sign up through your MND team, or ask them to refer you

studies.name: TIME
studies.blurb: Developing and evaluating TiM-Care, a remote monitoring system for people with MND and their carers.
studies.plain: In plain terms: not a drug. You use a monitoring tool from home and the team assesses whether it improves care. Very low burden and can be done entirely from the house.
studies.site: Remote — by phone, video or questionnaire
studies.apply: Sign up through your MND team, or ask them to refer you

studies.name: Exploring views of MND treatments
studies.blurb: Explores what matters most to people with MND when weighing up medications, to shape what drug developers aim at.
studies.plain: In plain terms: not a drug. A structured way of saying what a treatment would actually need to deliver to be worth taking — time, function, speech, independence. One session.
studies.site: Remote — by phone, video or questionnaire
studies.apply: Sign up through your MND team, or ask them to refer you

applyLinks.label: Exploring views of MND treatments study page

studies.name: Understanding preferences of drug treatments
studies.blurb: Measures the value people with MND place on different characteristics of a drug treatment. Listed as in set-up and opening soon.
studies.plain: In plain terms: not a drug. A trade-off exercise — how much side effect is worth how much benefit. Not open yet, so one to ask about later in the year.
studies.site: Remote — by phone, video or questionnaire
studies.apply: Not open yet — ask his MND team later in the year
